_comment: The nine areas of a life, and which of the twelve sectors feed each one.
A 'sector' is a 30-degree slice of the ecliptic counted from the Ascendant.
Astrology calls them houses; this product does not, because the whole voice
is astronomy-first and 'sector' is what they geometrically are. The reader
never sees the number: they see the area it belongs to.
Nine, not eight. Money used to sit inside Work, which followed the older
grouping of the 2nd, 6th and 10th sectors as one career axis. They are not
one thing: the 2nd is what you are worth and what you will trade time for,
the 6th is the daily work and the body doing it, the 10th is the public
standing that comes of both. Splitting the 2nd out gives money its own card
and leaves the grid at nine, which lays out three by three.
Sectors need a birth time. The Ascendant moves a degree every four minutes,
so a chart cast for noon has a sector layout that is wrong for 23 hours out
of 24. The Daily Sky refuses to guess and asks for the time instead.
Three names per area, and each has one job. 'label' is the full name and
heads a card. 'tab' is the one-word form for anywhere a full name will not
fit; keep it to a single word, and to one the copy validator's stop list
already holds, or the voice suite will read it as an invented proper noun.
'domain' is the clause that says why a reading landed here, written to
complete the sentence 'your Mars sits in ...'.
